_source: Modern MBA long video 'Why Buffets Suddenly Disappeared', 839K views, 38.5 min. Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-19 (speed pass per owner): frames at 0/2/5/9/14/20/30/45/60 s, then seeks at 320/716-722 (document burst)/1200 (sponsor)/1500/1700/2295 s; the first 12 s of captions read live (~30 words in 11 s, about 165 words a minute). No audio probe on this one. Our own descriptions; shots after 60 s are spot samples.

lines.gist: Places the story in the buffet's best decades.
A cheap fixed price bought unlimited comfort food in every town.
Lists the big chains and what their counters offered.
Casinos used buffets to pull visitors; the big-box buffet looked like the future.
A private-equity buyout loads the leading chain with debt.
Supermarkets could reuse leftover food; buffets had to throw it away.
Sums up why one survivor ended up owning the whole category.

ending.lastFrame: archival food footage into a YouTube end screen

whyItWorks: Almost the whole film is period TV ads and news footage, so every claim sits in its own era and feels like evidence.
Old 4:3 clips fill a 16:9 frame with a blurred copy of themselves behind, plus a small fixed corner watermark.
Newspaper clippings are shown whole and still, long enough to read the headline, as proof of each turning point.
Calm, steady narration with very few effects: the footage carries the energy, the voice carries the argument.
